title: Workspace KPI page: trend charts from the last 30 days
description:
Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour). One PR. Runs after LIN-3710 ("Public /kpis: trend charts and a shared chart helper").

## Why

The in-app workspace KPI page is all numbers and no charts. John, 20 Oct:

> "It's nicer to see charts showing how things change. Things like tasks done per day, total tasks, as well as harbours metrics, all tell the user what's going on."

> "There's maby a bit too much text, and some of the cumulative charts might be better as rates rather than totals (or we can toggle between)."

This ticket adds the trend charts the existing data supports, as rates. It runs AFTER the ticket "Public /kpis: trend charts and a shared chart helper", which creates `public/chart-helpers.js` (global `HarbourCharts`). This ticket reuses it. Showing a workspace its own cost on its login-gated KPI page is settled; the public page stays without cost (LIN-3703).

## What is true now

Checked at origin/main 8f39afd8.

* The page is server-rendered with no charts and no page script: `lib/render-workspace-kpis.js:114` (styles: `/style.css`, `/common-actions.css`, `/escalation-kpis.css`) and `:117` (scripts: `/common.js`, `/app.js`). Sections: activity (:47), funnel (:61), kinds (:72), stored (:81); the empty line is at :100-102. Route: `routes/workspace-kpis.js:29`.
* `collectWorkspaceKpis` (`lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js:42`) reads only this workspace, all filtered by `urlKey` (:47-54), from `readHorizonStart(now)` (:45, 30 days). It runs `summarizeActivity` twice (:57-58) and keeps only `.totals` (:65), so the per-day data is thrown away.
* `summarizeActivity` (`lib/kpi-stats.js:852`) already holds the per-day proxy phases (`proxy.daily.phases`, `PROXY_PHASES` :74) and the windowed dispatch and agent-status docs. `countByDay` (:153) is private. `buildDispatchByDay` (:639) is private, gives per-day top-kinds plus 'other', and its kind limit is the constant `DISPATCH_DAY_KIND_LIMIT = 5` (:72, used :640).
* `agentActions` total = proxy calls plus agent-status reports (:852 onward). Its daily series must add both.
* Lineages: `groupDispatchLineages` (`lib/dispatch-lineage.js:158`) gives `status`, `statusMs` (set at :236-238), `earliest`, `rowUsage`. `status === 'done'` comes from the agent's done marker, not a verified merge.
* The public page embeds its view via `embeddedData` and loads `['/chart.umd.min.js', '/kpis.js']` (`lib/render-kpis.js:191-192`). Chart.js is vendored at `public/chart.umd.min.js`.
* The canvas height rule `.kpi-chart-canvas` lives only in `public/kpis.css:142-151`, and the helper's `draw` turns off `maintainAspectRatio`. This page does not load `kpis.css`, so a canvas here would have no height.
* `tests/unit/kpi-stats-reads-pin.test.js` snapshots every read `collectKpiStats` makes. Workspace tests: `tests/unit/workspace-kpi-stats.test.js`, `render-workspace-kpis.test.js`, `tests/e2e/workspace-kpis.spec.js`, and `workspaceKpis` in `tests/helpers.js:105,146`.

## Design (fixed choices)

All charts cover the existing 30-day read horizon. No new read horizon, no new collection, no change to any read. Keep every existing test id and section.

Rules:

* Less text. Each chart: a short title and at most one plain "what it shows" line. Derivation notes go in a collapsed "Show the numbers" disclosure beside the data table.
* Rates only. No rate/total toggle is visible on this page.
* Existing page shell, tokens and vendored Chart.js. Load `embeddedData` plus `['/chart.umd.min.js', '/chart-helpers.js', '/workspace-kpis.js']` (a new page script), then `/common.js` and `/app.js`. Copy the `.kpi-chart-canvas` height rule (`kpis.css:142-151`) into `public/escalation-kpis.css`; do not load `/kpis.css`.
* No-JS fallback: the numbers tables render on the server inside the disclosure (native `<details>`), and a `<noscript>` line says charts need JavaScript.

Charts (series come from `collectWorkspaceKpis`, all UTC days; ids B3, B5 and B6 are not in this ticket):

1. **B1 tiles with sparklines.** The three activity cards (dispatches, autopilot runs, agent actions) get a 30-day sparkline. `feedbackNotes` gets none. Series: `countByDay` over `windowedDispatchDocs` (export it); autopilot = same filtered to `kind === 'autopilot'`; agent actions = proxy phases summed per day plus `countByDay` of agent-status docs. Each series sums to that card's 30d value.
2. **B2 "Tasks done per day".** `groupDispatchLineages([...historyDocs, ...queueDocs])`, count `status === 'done'` by UTC day of `statusMs`. Line: "Tasks the agent marked done, by day." Rate only; the running total comes with the rollup tickets. Disclosure notes: "done" is the agent's done marker, not a verified merge; tasks that started before the horizon may be partly seen.
3. **B4 "Runs by kind per week".** Fold the per-day kind counts into four 7-day buckets ending today (the last 28 days); top 3 kinds plus 'other'. This needs a limit parameter on `buildDispatchByDay` (export it); its default stays 5 so the public page is unchanged. Stacked bar. The oldest 2 days of the horizon are in no bucket; the disclosure says so.
4. **B7 "Cost per day".** Titled "API-equivalent cost", its own section, a normal part of the page. Rate only. `reduceLineageCost` (`lib/terminal-marked-task-cost.js:138`) returns `costUsd`, `priced`, `fullyPriced`. `windowedSpend` (`lib/weekly-budget.js:121`, not exported; export it) already buckets fully-priced lineage cost by the UTC day of `earliest`, skips `status === 'skipped'` (:129), and counts `lineageCount`/`pricedCount`. Use it over the same lineages: cost by the day the task STARTED, `skipped` excluded, unpriced never $0. Show "priced N of M tasks" (`pricedCount`, `lineageCount`). No on/off switch or flag.

New test ids: `workspace-kpis-section-{done-per-day|runs-by-kind|cost}`, `workspace-kpis-chart-<name>` (canvas), `workspace-kpis-numbers-<name>` (disclosure), `workspace-kpis-table-<name>`, `workspace-kpis-spark-<card>`. Trend sections follow the existing empty rule; kind labels are escaped.

## Done when

1. `public/chart-helpers.js` with `HarbourCharts.draw`, `.sparkline` and `.numbersTable` is on main. Check FIRST. If missing, STOP and report; do not write your own copy.
2. `collectWorkspaceKpis` returns the series above; each daily series sums to its 30d total.
3. The page shows the three sparklines and three chart sections (done per day, runs by kind, cost with "priced N of M tasks"), rates only, within the short-text rules.
4. Without JavaScript the tables are in the page and nothing is broken.
5. A test seeds two workspaces and proves no cross-workspace leakage in any new series (see Tests).
6. Rendering checks pass (below), and there is no horizontal scroll at 390px, light and dark.
7. Every read is still filtered to the one workspace; `collectKpiStats` reads and `kpi-stats-reads-pin.test.js` are unchanged.
8. `public/llms.txt` and the docs match the new DOM.

## Tests

* `tests/unit/workspace-kpi-stats.test.js` (extend, real MangoDB as the file does today): two workspaces in the same collections, each with different dispatches, kinds, done lineages, agent-status and priced usage. Each new series for `keyA` equals the single-workspace expectation; adding or changing `keyB` moves nothing in `keyA`; no `keyB` urlKey, issue identifier or prompt text appears in `keyA`'s output. Also: series sums match card totals; done counted on the `statusMs` day; the kind limit parameter gives top 3 plus 'other' while the default stays 5; cost skips unpriced and `skipped` and uses the start day.
* `tests/unit/render-workspace-kpis.test.js`: new sections, canvases, disclosures with tables, `<noscript>`, script order, a hostile kind escaped, the cost wording, the canvas height rule in `escalation-kpis.css`.
* `tests/unit/kpi-stats-reads-pin.test.js` passes unedited.
* `tests/e2e/workspace-kpis.spec.js` (seed through the app's dispatch API; add selectors to `SELECTORS.workspaceKpis`): with JS, each chart canvas has non-zero size; with `javaScriptEnabled: false`, tables are present and the page has no errors; at 390px `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= clientWidth` in light and `.theme-dark`. If a done or priced lineage cannot be created through the API, cover those in unit tests and say so in the PR.

## Docs

* `public/llms.txt:132-139` (this page's block): add the new test ids and one line per chart.
* `docs/architecture/source-map.md:39,:68` and the kpi-stats / workspace-kpi-stats entries: new series, exported helpers.
* Update the header comment of `lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js` ("counts and labels only") to say cost is this workspace's own API-equivalent estimate.
* CLAUDE.md: add nothing (110-line cap).

## Out of scope

* Running total since connecting (B3): needs a daily rollup. Follow-up.
* Time to merge (B5): needs PR times recorded. Follow-up.
* B6 follow-on runs: later ticket, needs an agreed definition.
* Any rate/total toggle; changes to the public /kpis page or its reads; a new read horizon or collection; cash figures; cost on the public page; a second chart helper.

## Operator notes

**Rules for this run**

* No live calls to outside services (GitHub, Linear, OpenRouter, [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) or any other live host). Tests use the existing fakes.
* No paid model or OpenRouter calls.
* This is one PR. Don't split it into child tickets.
* No parallel forks or background sub-agents; one part at a time.
* Targeted tests while iterating (`node --test tests/unit/<file>.test.js`). Full unit suite (`npm run test:unit`) once before opening the PR. Leave e2e to CI.
* A failing-then-passing test is the witness for any behaviour change.
* Keep every existing ticket reference and every reason comment beside the code it governs; drop one only if its code is gone, and list those in the PR.
* A new production file (anything outside `tests/` and `docs/`) gets a pattern in `scripts/code-shape/areas.json` for the area that owns it, in the same PR. First match wins there, so check the file lands in that area and not in "Other features": run `node scripts/code-shape/seams.mjs . <commit>` at the base commit and at your final commit, report the area-pair count both times, and give the reason for any new pair. If it cannot run in your checkout (exit 2, `acorn` missing), record it as not run.
* Prompt text (templates, meta-prompt, runner prompt) is size-frozen (`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`). If you add prompt text, remove bytes elsewhere or raise the ceiling with the reason recorded beside it (LIN-3633), and say which in the PR.
* Where a choice is still open, keep today's behaviour, write it up as an open question in the PR, and carry on. Never stop to wait for a person. A check that needs a live service or a person is recorded in the PR as not run (what, why, follow-up), not a reason to hold the close.

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2009](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2009>) (merged as `0da144c8`). The plan's design decisions (reuse of `buildDailyDone` and a shared `proxyCallsByDay`, `numbersTable` not used on this page, top-3 kinds ranked over the 28 covered days, the cost window running to the end of the day axis, the CSS rules copied alongside the canvas height rule) all landed as written; the only deviation was the seams baseline, which is 61 area-pair links (the plan's 65 was a miscount), unchanged by the PR.

The plan fits one session. plan-review due: no.

The full pre-prune description (plan, risks, scope assessment, open questions) is preserved in the task snapshots, and the review and close-out comments carry the history.

comments.body: LIN-3710 has merged and deployed (`c1d5c700`): `public/chart-helpers.js` now exposes exactly `HarbourCharts.draw`, `sparkline` and `numbersTable` (classic script, no page strings). `trailingMean` is not exported; it is passed to a `build(canvas, tools)` callback, so reuse it from there or ask for a fourth export. Reference wiring: `public/kpis.js`; disclosure markup: `lib/render-kpis.js`. Also see LIN-3715 for the 390px overflow-test idiom (`expectNoClippedOverflow` in `tests/e2e/kpis.spec.js`) before you write a mobile check.

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2009 (head 17cbd1c3). CI green: unit, 4 E2E shards, secret scan.

Workspace KPI page now has 3 card sparklines and 3 chart sections (done per day, runs by kind per week, API-equivalent cost with "priced N of M tasks"), rates only, from the existing 30-day reads. Numbers tables are server-rendered in `<details>` with a `<noscript>` line. Reuses `public/chart-helpers.js`; public `/kpis` and `kpi-stats-reads-pin.test.js` untouched.

- Tests: `npm run test:unit` 18947 pass / 0 fail. New tests fail on main (8 render tests, stats file fails to load) and pass with the change. Two-workspace leakage test covers every new series.
- Done/priced lineages can't be seeded through the dispatch API, so those series are unit-only; E2E checks page shape, no-JS, and 390px overflow in light and dark.
- Seams link count 61 at base and at final commit.
- Open question left at default: no 7-day mean line on done-per-day.

## Review — LIN-3711

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2009, reviewed at head `17cbd1c3` (base `d10e7398`; main has since moved to `8ddb0f3b`, LIN-3722, which touches none of these files; PR is MERGEABLE).

CI: green on `17cbd1c3`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success.

### Scope vs plan
The PR matches the plan's file list exactly: 12 files, no file outside the plan. Gate 1 is met: `public/chart-helpers.js` is used, and the PR adds no second chart helper. The page script uses only `draw` and `sparkline`, as plan item 3 says.
- `collectKpiStats`: no read changes. The PR only adds exports, and `proxyCallsByDay` replaces an inline expression with the same arithmetic. `buildDispatchByDay` still defaults its limit to 5. `kpi-stats-reads-pin.test.js` is unedited and passes.
- Every new series is built from the six `urlKey`-filtered reads that already existed. There is no new read and no new horizon.
- Seams: **61 links at base and at head, no new pair.** Platform → Runs imports went from 8 to 10, which the plan predicted. The plan's "65 baseline" was a miscount; the PR's 61 is right.
- No rulings exist for LIN-3711.

### Regression check
`git log -- <touched files>`: the only earlier fix in this area is LIN-2273 (`50595c61`, weekly-budget `byDay` day-key basis). The PR only adds `export` to `windowedSpend` and leaves its semantics untouched. The workspace axis uses the same UTC `YYYY-MM-DD` basis, pinned by the 23:59Z/00:00Z test. Mutation M13 below confirms that test goes red on a key mismatch. No reverts touch these files.

### Tests: mutation check (each mutation reverted afterwards)
I ran `node --test` on the workspace-kpi-stats, render-workspace-kpis and kpi-stats test files. All pass unmutated.

Each mutation below **went red**:
- M1: rank kinds over 30 days instead of 28.
- M3: count done on the start day.
- M4: drop agent-status from agent actions.
- M5: drop the autopilot filter.
- M6: wrong `foldWeeks` offset.
- M7: `buildDispatchByDay` default limit set to 3 (the public `collectKpiStats` test goes red).
- M8: stop excluding `skipped` lineages.
- M9: unescaped table cells.
- M10: embed data on the empty page.
- M11: `$0` shown when nothing is priced.
- M12: no `<$0.01` floor.
- M13: wrong cost day key.
- M14: `proxyCallsByDay` drops a phase.

**Stayed green: M2.** I changed the `windowedSpend` upper bound from `activityStart + 30d` back to `now`. The test comment says "a dispatch inside the final day is not dropped", but its fixture dispatches at 09:00Z with `now` at 12:00Z, so it never exercises plan item 5. See ledger item 1.

The test levels fit the change: the series are unit-tested on a real MangoDB, two-workspace leakage included, and the renderer has unit tests. The e2e tests cover canvas or empty-note size, the no-JS context with zero page errors, and 390px in light and `.theme-dark` (the hook is on `<html>`, per `public/style.css:7`).

### Isolated, or one of a class?
I checked the class "every series on this page and where it is bucketed" (sparklines, done/day, runs by kind, cost/day). All of it lives in `buildDaily`, and every series shares the 30-day axis; the sum tests are the witness. For the day-key-basis class, `windowedSpend`'s `dayKeyOf` and `windows.days` match. The weekly gauge's 06:00Z enumeration is unchanged and outside this ticket. No sibling is left unhandled, so the change is isolated.

### Non-blocking nits (close-out may take or leave them)
- In `public/workspace-kpis.js`, the cost tooltip prints `$0.00` for a sub-half-cent day, while the table prints `<$0.01`. The y-axis tick also prints `$0.5` rather than `$0.50`.

### What CI Did Not Prove
1. **Inside** (plan item 5, a claim this change depends on): the cost window runs to the end of today's axis, so a lineage whose `earliest` is at or after `now` is still bucketed. No test witnesses this (mutation M2 stays green).
   - **Settle before merge.** In `tests/unit/workspace-kpi-stats.test.js`, test "cost: by the start day…", add a priced lineage with `dispatchedAt: NOW` (2026-06-10T12:00Z, e.g. cost 0.5). Change the assertions to `perDay[29] === 0.75`, sum `2.25`, `pricedCount 3`, `lineageCount 8`, and reword the comment to "a dispatch stamped exactly now is not dropped".
   - **Distinguishing condition:** the test must go red when the third argument of `windowedSpend` in `lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js` is replaced with `now.getTime()`.
2. **Inside** (the B2 and B7 charts as drawn): drawn done-per-day and cost canvases with real data. E2E can only seed dispatch-only data, because `[done]` and `[usage]` entries come from the runner, as the PR states. So in CI those two charts only ever render their empty note. Canvas height comes from the same `.kpi-chart-canvas` rule, which runs-by-kind proves.
   - **Settle after deploy.** On a workspace that has at least one done and one priced lineage in the last 30 days, open `/workspace/<key>/kpis`. Both canvases should be drawn (not the "○ …" note) with height > 0, and the cost bars and "priced N of M tasks" should match the "Show the numbers" table.
3. **Inside** (short-text and visual rules): how the charts look, meaning legend legibility and colour contrast in dark mode at 390px. Only a person can judge this.
   - **Settle after deploy,** during the same visit as item 2.
4. **Discharged** (an outside producer contract): the `[done]` marker and `[usage]` feedback producers. This page reuses `buildDailyDone`, `reduceLineageCost` and `windowedSpend` unchanged, and those already consume both producers in production (public `/kpis` `daily.done` and the cost fold).

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger.

The deliverable meets every "Done when" item. The public page and the reads pin are unchanged. 13 of 14 mutations go red. The one gap is a missing witness for the cost-window bound, and close-out can add it in one test edit (ledger item 1) before merging. Items 2–3 are post-deploy checks.

## Close-out — LIN-3711

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2009, squash commit `0da144c8` (pinned with `--match-head-commit a322ec48`). Production deployment of `0da144c8` reported success; the live `/workspace-kpis.js` contains the final fix.

**Verdict used:** review's Approve at `17cbd1c3`, conditional on the ledger.

### Changes I made after approval (nobody reviewed these)
- `465cd34d` answers ledger item 1. In `tests/unit/workspace-kpi-stats.test.js`, the cost test now adds a priced lineage at `dispatchedAt: NOW` (cost 0.5), with `perDay[29] === 0.75`, sum `2.25`, `pricedCount 3`, `lineageCount 8` and the comment reworded, as review specified. The distinguishing condition ran: replacing the third argument of `windowedSpend` with `windows.nowMs` (the in-scope equivalent of `now.getTime()`) turns exactly that test red (actual 0.25, expected 0.75); the source was restored.
- `a322ec48` answers review's non-blocking nit. In `public/workspace-kpis.js`, the cost tooltip shows `<$0.01` for a sub-half-cent day like the table, and y ticks print two decimals (`$0.50`). Display only; no data change.

### Ledger
1. **Cost window bound (inside): settled before merge** by `465cd34d` and the mutation run above.
2. **Done/cost canvases with real data (inside, post-deploy): not run.** The page is login-gated, I have no workspace session, and E2E cannot seed `[done]`/`[usage]` lineages. The operator can run it on any workspace with at least one done and one priced lineage in the last 30 days: both canvases drawn with height > 0, and cost bars plus "priced N of M tasks" matching the table. No monitor covers it. Recorded on the PR as well.
3. **Short-text/visual rules, legend legibility and dark-mode contrast at 390px (inside, post-deploy): not run.** Only a person can judge it; same visit as item 2.
4. **`[done]`/`[usage]` producers (discharged by review):** nothing to do.

### CI
Green on the exact merged head `a322ec48`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success. Local `npm run test:unit`: 18947 pass, 0 fail.

### Housekeeping
- Related tickets: LIN-3724 (rollup) and LIN-3713 (PR times) are the homes for the deferred B3/B5 charts and stay open; LIN-3723 and LIN-3705 are unrelated. None settled by this work, so none closed.
- Outside follow-ups: none. Review's ledger had no outside items; the one nit was fixed here. No rulings exist for this ticket.
- Description archived (snapshot verified: full 25,903-character pre-prune description) and the implementation plan pruned to a stub; the original problem, design, tests, docs and operator notes are kept.
